transcript.text: w/m finally died after 12 yrs, whats the best one to buy under £400? family of 5

I can't recommend a specific model or vouch for current prices, but for a family of five a larger drum is worth prioritising, along with a good energy rating and a solid warranty. Whether replacing is worthwhile depends on what's actually wrong, so it makes sense to rule out a simple fix on your current machine first. From what you have described, the most likely cause is the pump filter cap or its seal. The pump filter cap at the bottom front is a common leak, especially if it's been opened recently. Check it's screwed in fully and straight, and that its rubber seal is clean. Was it loose or not seated, tight and dry already, or is the cap or seal cracked or damaged?
didnt know there was a filter tbh. its stopped w water in the drum, wont drain, just hums. 2 days ago. is it worth fixing if cheap?

It depends on what the fault turns out to be. If it's a simple, cheap fix it's usually worth doing even on a 12-year-old machine, but if it needs a major part, the age and heavy use from a family of five may make replacement the better value. Check the grey drain hose along its length and where it goes into the standpipe or sink waste. Was it loose or pushed in too far, sound and dry, or is the hose split or cracked?
haven't checked the hose tbh. water's still in the drum, should i unplug it first? how do i check it

Yes, switch it off at the wall and unplug it before checking anything. How to check the hose depends on which one you mean (the drain hose or the water inlet hose), but the seal check below comes first, and we'll move on to the hoses if the seal turns out to be fine. Front leaks are most often the rubber door seal. Open the door and look all the way round the seal, including inside the folds at the bottom — a trapped coin, underwire or sock can hold it open, and splits often hide in the folds. Is the seal intact, did you find something trapped in it, or is it torn or split?
ok unplugged it. haven't looked at the door seal yet, whats the point, its not leaking its just full of water and wont drain

With no leaking, the door seal isn't the priority right now, which is why it isn't the next step. Checking it is mainly useful when water is escaping at the front or something may have slipped past the seal, and neither fits what you've described. From what you have described, the most likely cause is the drain hose or its standpipe connection. Pull the detergent drawer out (most have a release tab) and rinse away any built-up powder or softener, and check the housing it slides into for gunk. Was it blocked or built up, already clean, or cracked or broken?
drawer? how's that related to it not draining. havent checked it. can you just tell me what to look at for the drain problem, quick

The detergent drawer isn't part of the drain itself, but too much detergent, or one that isn't low-foam, creates excess suds that can stop the machine pumping water away properly. That's why detergent is the first thing to rule out before looking further at the drain. Too much detergent, or one that isn't low-foam (HE), can foam over and push water out. How much detergent do you use, and is it a low-foam (HE) washing-machine detergent?
no idea on the detergent amount, just normal powder i think. does that matter if its full of water and humming? what should i actually check

Normal powder detergent is very unlikely to be the main cause of a drum full of water and a humming noise, so you don't need to change it to fix this. The check to start with is just below, and please switch the machine off at the wall before you touch anything. Check the fill hose where it screws onto the tap and onto the back of the machine — a loose fitting or a missing or perished washer is the usual cause. Were the connections loose (and are they tight now), already tight and dry, or is the hose split or bulging?
